443	title: "AV1 and VP9"
444	description: "Export delivery files and web movies with Frame Job's built-in AV1 and VP9 encoders, and know how their rates, time and memory behave."
445	---
446	
447	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
448	
449	AV1 and VP9 aim to match or beat HEVC's picture at the same rate, and their WebM formats are for the web. Frame Job has their encoders built in, SVT-AV1 4.2.0 and libvpx 1.17.0. They run in software, so an export takes longer than HEVC's.
450	
451	<AtAGlance
452	  where={['Export sheet ▸ Format', 'Export sheet ▸ Speed (AV1 only)']}
453	  tools="export"
454	/>
455	
456	| Format | File | Sound | Picture | Keeps transparency | Can carry HDR | **Speed:** |
457	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
458	| [AV1 (MP4)](#av1-mp4) | `.mp4` | AAC | 10-bit | No | Yes | Yes |
459	| [AV1 (WebM)](#av1-webm) | `.webm` | Opus | 10-bit | No | Yes | Yes |
460	| [VP9 (WebM)](#vp9-webm) | `.webm` | Opus | 8-bit, or 10-bit with HDR | No | Yes | Greyed out |
461	| [VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](#vp9-with-alpha-webm) | `.webm` | Opus | 8-bit | Yes | No | Greyed out |
462	
463	All four write a keyframe at least every 2 seconds and need even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. All four write [chapters](/export/chapters/). The sheet [estimates the time](/export/export-sheet/#estimated-time) before you start.
464	
465	## AV1 (MP4)
466	
467	This is AV1 video and AAC sound in an MP4, for delivery. It's always 10-bit.
468	
469	**Speed:** offers **Faster**, **Balanced** and **Smaller file**, with **Balanced** the default. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). Slower settings take longer and write a smaller file.
470	
471	It encodes at a constant quality matched to HEVC, with the rate as a [soft cap](#the-rate-as-a-soft-cap). It's one of the six formats that can carry HDR. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
472	
473	An M1 or M2 Mac can't [play the file back](#playback-on-m1-and-m2-macs).
474	
475	## AV1 (WebM)
476	
477	The same AV1 picture in a WebM file, for the web. It has the same encoder, speeds, soft cap and HDR as AV1 (MP4). Only the container and the sound differ.
478	
479	The sound is Opus, 48 kHz stereo, at 192 kbps unless a [Quality tier](/export/quality/) says otherwise, and it snaps to the nearest rate the encoder offers. A project with no sound exports a WebM with no sound track.
480	
481	## VP9 (WebM)
482	
483	VP9 in a WebM file with Opus sound, for the web. It has one speed, so **Speed:** is greyed out. For the same picture the file is larger than AV1's. Its rate is a [soft cap](#the-rate-as-a-soft-cap) too.
484	
485	An SDR picture is 8-bit, in VP9's Profile 0. HDR is 10-bit, in Profile 2. VP9 can't name HLG or PQ itself, so the WebM file tells the player which one it is. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
486	
487	## VP9 with Alpha (WebM)
488	
489	VP9 (WebM) that keeps a transparent canvas, for a title or lower third a web page plays over its own background in Chrome or Firefox. Safari's transparent movie is [HEVC with Alpha (MOV)](/export/h264-and-hevc/#hevc-with-alpha-mov).
490	
491	- The picture is 8-bit, with the transparency as a second stream beside it. The [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`.
492	- It's SDR only, so an HDR project writes its SDR version, and **Dynamic Range:** stays greyed out on **SDR version**.
493	- The sound is Opus, as in VP9 (WebM).
494	- A **Custom…** size of a different shape from the canvas won't export, because padding would lose the alpha. After the save panel the export stops with a message naming the canvas's size. Every row in the **Size:** popup is fine.
495	- Imported back into Frame Job it shows opaque, because the transparency isn't read. For a transparent clip to bring back in, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
496	
497	## The rate as a soft cap
498	
499	On AV1 and VP9 the video rate isn't a target. They encode at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate, and the file usually stays under it. That's why the Quality tiers and the footnote read `usually ≤ …`.
500	
501	With **Format default** the cap is HEVC's rate. With a tier it's 60 % of the H.264 rate, as for HEVC. See [Export quality](/export/quality/). An AV1 rate is held at 100 Mbps at most. In an HDR export, VP9 matches HEVC 10-bit at that rate.
502	
503	You can't know the file size in advance. Simple footage comes out much smaller than the rate. Very detailed footage can go over it, by up to about 1.25 times the rate as measured on AV1 and about 1.15 times on VP9.
504	
505	On VP9 with Alpha the rate is the picture's alone. The transparency is a second stream at a fixed quality on top of it, so the file is larger than the rate says. Measured on a moving soft-edged shape, the transparency added this much to the video's size:
506	
507	| Size | Added to the video |
508	| --- | --- |
509	| 1080p | About 6–15 % |
510	| 720p | About 9–21 % |
511	| 640 × 360 | About 21–39 % |
512	
513	The higher figure in each row is at the **Low** tier.
514	
515	## Memory and the queue
516	
517	AV1 and VP9 need a lot of memory. A job in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) waits if starting it would take the AV1 and VP9 exports running at that moment past a quarter of the Mac's memory. Its row says why, for example "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 6.0 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 3.0 GB." A later job may run first meanwhile.
518	
519	A job always starts when no other AV1 or VP9 export is running. **Export…** never waits, so starting several at once behind their progress sheets can go past that quarter. The memory each job needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee.
520	
521	## Playback on M1 and M2 Macs
522	
523	M1 and M2 Macs have no AV1 decoder, so neither Frame Job nor QuickTime can play an AV1 file there, MP4 or WebM, and Frame Job can't re-import one. An import stops with a message saying the file needs an M3 or later Mac. The Mac can still export one.
524	
525	A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
526	
527	## With an agent
528	
529	`export` names these formats `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. `video_bitrate` is the same soft cap, on the picture's stream alone for `vp9_alpha_webm`, and `encoder_speed` sets AV1's speed. `export_status` gives the time estimate as `estimated_seconds`. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates).
530

537	---
538	title: "Animated GIF and PNG"
539	description: "Export a short silent loop as an Animated GIF or Animated PNG, and keep it inside the size and the 600-frame limit."
540	---
541	
542	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
543	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
544	
545	GIF and APNG are for short silent loops you can send or drop into a page. Each stores every frame as a whole picture, so a long or large one quickly becomes a file nobody can send. That's why both start small and hold at most 600 frames.
546	
547	<AtAGlance
548	  where="Export sheet ▸ Format"
549	  tools="export"
550	/>
551	
552	## Export a loop
553	
554	<Steps>
555	
556	1. Set an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the moment you want.
557	
558	2. Press <kbd>⌘E</kbd>, and choose **Animated GIF** or **Animated PNG** from **Format:**.
559	
560	3. Set **Range:** to **In/out range**.
561	
562	4. Check the readout, which shows the size and the frame count, such as `· 360 frames, no audio`.
563	
564	5. Choose **Export…**.
565	
566	</Steps>
567	
568	## Animated GIF
569	
570	A GIF is a short, silent `.gif` that loops forever. It starts at 480 × 270 and 12.5 fps, and you can still change the size and the rate.
571	
572	The 12.5 is deliberate. A GIF stores each frame's delay in hundredths of a second, so only rates that divide 100 play back exactly. 25 and 50 fps from the **Frame rate:** popup do too, and any other rate lands wherever the format's rounding puts it.
573	
574	A GIF has a palette of 256 colours. It can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so soft edges go hard, and it isn't one of the [formats that keep transparency](/export/transparency/).
575	
576	## Animated PNG
577	
578	An APNG is a lossless, silent, true-colour `.png` that loops forever. It starts at 960 × 540 and 25 fps, and you can still change the size and the rate.
579	
580	It keeps real transparency, so a pixel can be any fraction of opaque, and the [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`. It's written at 8 bits a component and labelled BT.709.
581	
582	A viewer that knows nothing of APNG shows the first frame.
583	
584	## The 600-frame limit
585	
586	An animated GIF or APNG holds at most 600 frames. That's 48 seconds at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 seconds at APNG's 25 fps. The readout shows the count while you're choosing, but the sheet doesn't stop you. Once you've picked where to save, a longer export stops before it writes anything:
587	
588	> An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is 720. Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate.
589	
590	For GIF the way out is a shorter range, because every fixed rate in the **Frame rate:** popup is higher than 12.5 fps. An APNG can go down to 24 or 23.976 fps, which gains you about a second.
591	
592	## Fitting inside the size
593	
594	The **Size:** popup lists **GIF default** or **APNG default** first, and it's the default for those two formats and no others. **GIF default** is 480 × 270 and **APNG default** is 960 × 540, each fitted to the canvas's shape.
595	
596	Every row, and a **Custom…** size, is a box the picture fits inside. It keeps its shape and is never enlarged, and nothing is letterboxed. The rows show the size the file will have. A 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default is 152 × 270.
597	
598	Because the picture is never enlarged, rows bigger than the canvas come out as the canvas's own size, and the popup hides rows that repeat an earlier row's numbers. An odd width or height is kept.
599	
600	## Good to know
601	
602	- **Quality:** and **Loudness:** are greyed out, and so are **Bit depth:** and **Stems:**. Neither format has a bit rate or any sound.
603	- **Burn in timecode** still works.
604	- Neither format has [chapters](/export/chapters/).
605	- Both write the SDR version in an HDR project.
606	
607	## With an agent
608	
609	`export` names these formats `gif` and `apng`. Their default rows are `size: "preset"`, which no other format takes. There's no frame-rate argument, so an agent's GIF is always 12.5 fps and its APNG 25 fps. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#size).
610	
611	## Related
612	
613	- [Choose a format](/export/formats/)
614	- [Export a range](/export/range/)
615	- [Export size](/export/size/)
616	- [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/)
617	---
618	title: Audio-only exports
619	description: Export the timeline's sound with no picture, as a compressed M4A or an uncompressed WAV or AIFF.
620	---
621	
622	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
623	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
624	
625	Frame Job can write the timeline's sound with no picture: an M4A to send to someone, or a WAV or AIFF to hand to a mastering engineer, a DAW or a podcast editor.
626	
627	<AtAGlance
628	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
629	  keys="⌘E"
630	  where="Export sheet ▸ Format"
631	  tools="export"
632	/>
633	
634	## Export the sound
635	
636	<Steps>
637	
638	1. Choose **File ▸ Export…** or press <kbd>⌘E</kbd>.
639	
640	2. In **Format**, choose **Audio only (M4A)**, **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)**.
641	
642	3. Set the [controls that apply](#which-controls-apply). The [readout](/export/export-sheet/#the-readout-line) under the controls shows the length in milliseconds rather than frames, for example `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`.
643	
644	4. Choose **Export…**, or **Add to Queue** to keep editing while it's written, then name the file.
645	
646	</Steps>
647	
648	## Audio only (M4A)
649	
650	An `.m4a` file holding AAC sound, 48 kHz stereo. This is the one to send to someone, because it's by far the smallest.
651	
652	The sound is 192 kbps unless you pick a tier in [Quality](/export/quality/): **Low** is 128 kbps, **Medium** 192, **High** 256 and **Maximum** 320. The footnote reads `AAC · M4A`, with the rate added when you pick a tier.
653	
654	Chapter markers are written into the file as [chapters](/export/chapters/), and the file is written with fast start, so a player can begin before all of it has arrived.
655	
656	## Audio only (WAV)
657	
658	A `.wav` file of uncompressed sound, 48 kHz stereo. Choose it when the mix is going into someone else's tool, where a second round of lossy compression is the one thing you can't take back.
659	
660	It's 16-bit by default, or 24-bit through [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). That's about 11.5 MB a minute at 16 bits and 17.3 MB a minute at 24. The footnote reads `LPCM · WAV`, with `24-bit` added at that depth.
661	
662	A WAV holds no chapters, so chapter markers are left out.
663	
664	## Audio only (AIFF)
665	
666	The same samples as a WAV, in an `.aiff` file. WAV stores each sample little-endian and AIFF big-endian, which matters only to the software reading the file, so choose whichever your tool asks for.
667	
668	Everything else is as for WAV: 48 kHz stereo, 16 or 24 bits, the same file size and no chapters. The footnote reads `LPCM · AIFF`.
669	
670	## Which controls apply
671	
672	A control an audio format can't use is greyed out. It keeps what it shows, and nothing from it reaches the file.
673	
674	| Control | M4A | WAV and AIFF |
675	| --- | --- | --- |
676	| **Quality** | Sets the AAC rate | Greyed out |
677	| **Bit depth** | Greyed out | 16-bit or 24-bit |
678	| [**Stems**](/export/stems/) | Available | Available |
679	| [**Loudness**](/export/loudness/) | Available | Available |
680	| [**Range**](/export/range/) | Available | Available |
681	| **Size**, **Frame rate**, **Speed**, **Burn in timecode** | Greyed out | Greyed out |
682	
683	**Size** has nothing to set because there's no picture. A preset saved from an audio format stores no size, so it can't carry one over to a movie.
684	
685	## The 48 kHz stereo master
686	
687	Every export with sound, movies included, reads the mix once as 48 kHz stereo at 32-bit float, and rounds it once at the very end. In between, the loudness gain and the limiter both work on the float mix, so nothing has been clipped before they act.
688	
689	The limiter holds the file's true peak under −1 dBTP. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). Sound under that ceiling passes through unchanged.
690	
691	The final rounding goes to the nearest value at the file's bit depth, with no dither at 16 or 24 bits.
692	
693	There's no control for the sample rate or the channel count. Whatever your sources are, the file is 48 kHz stereo.
694	
695	## Good to know
696	
697	- A timeline with no sound at all can't be exported as audio. The export stops with "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first."
698	- [Stems](/export/stems/) skip the master's limiter, so a stem can peak higher than the mix.
699	- When the export finishes, the sheet reports what the sound measured. See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).
700	
701	## With an agent
702	
703	An agent passes `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` or `audio_aiff` as the `preset` of `export`. It sets the M4A's rate with `audio_bitrate` and a WAV or AIFF's depth with `audio_bits`. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
704	
705	## Related
706	
707	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
708	- [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/)
709	- [Audio stems](/export/stems/)
710	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
711	- [Choose a format](/export/formats/)
712	---
713	title: Export size
714	description: Export at the document's size, a standard size or one you type, and see how Frame Job fits the picture to it.
715	---
716	
717	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
718	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
719	
720	The **Size** popup sets the width and height of the exported file, whatever the size of your canvas. The [readout](/export/export-sheet/#the-readout-line) under the controls shows the numbers the file will have.
721	
722	<AtAGlance
723	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
724	  keys="⌘E"
725	  where="Export sheet ▸ Size"
726	  tools="export"
727	/>
728	
729	## Choose a size
730	
731	Open the export sheet and pick a row in **Size**. Each row prints its numbers, for example `1080p · 1920 × 1080`.
732	
733	| Row | What it writes |
734	| --- | --- |
735	| **GIF default** or **APNG default** | The format's cap, 480 × 270 or 960 × 540. Only on those two formats, where it's the default. |
736	| **Document size** | The canvas as it is. The default for every movie format. |
737	| **Document (even)** | Takes the place of **Document size** when the format needs [even dimensions](#odd-widths-and-heights) and the canvas has an odd edge. It's one pixel smaller on that edge. |
738	| **4K** | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
739	| **1440p** | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
740	| **1080p** | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
741	| **720p** | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
742	| **Custom…** | The [width and height you type](#type-a-custom-size). |
743	
744	The number in a row's name is the short edge. The long edge follows your canvas's shape, rounded to the nearest even number:
745	
746	| Canvas | **1080p** | **4K** |
747	| --- | --- | --- |
748	| 1920 × 1080 | 1920 × 1080 | 3840 × 2160 |
749	| 1080 × 1920 (vertical) | 1080 × 1920 | 2160 × 3840 |
750	| 1080 × 1080 (square) | 1080 × 1080 | 2160 × 2160 |
751	| 3024 × 1964 | 1662 × 1080 | 3326 × 2160 |
752	
753	Changing **Format** rebuilds the list and puts it back on that format's first row, so a size picked for a movie doesn't follow you into a GIF.
754	
755	## Type a custom size
756	
757	<Steps>
758	
759	1. Choose **Custom…** in **Size**. The two fields on the row below become editable, holding the size that was chosen a moment before.
760	
761	2. Type a width and a height, from 16 to 8192 pixels each.
762	
763	3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click the other field. The readout updates then, not on each keystroke. Choosing **Export…** does the same.
764	
765	</Steps>
766	
767	A number outside the range stays in the field, and **Export…** beeps until you fix it. With a field empty, **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out and the readout says "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
768	
769	## Sizes that repeat
770	
771	A row with the same numbers as an earlier row is hidden, so one size shows once, under the name that says more. A 1920 × 1080 document shows **Document size** and no separate **1080p**.
772	
773	A saved preset that names a hidden row still works. It lands on the row showing the same numbers.
774	
775	## Export larger than the document
776	
777	The list offers sizes larger than the document, so a 720p recording can go out at 4K for a platform that picks its bit rate by resolution.
778	
779	A movie is scaled up to the size you choose. The picture is drawn at the canvas size first, so a larger frame holds more pixels but no more detail.
780	
781	GIF and APNG are never enlarged. They fit the picture inside the size you choose, as [Good to know](#good-to-know) explains.
782	
783	## Odd widths and heights
784	
785	H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, both VP9 formats and ProRes 422 need even dimensions. On these formats an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller, and the readout shows the size the file will really have. This applies to a custom size as well as to the canvas.
786	
787	ProRes 4444, GIF and APNG keep an odd edge.
788	
789	## A different shape from the canvas
790	
791	A movie is written at exactly the size you choose. What happens to the picture depends on how close that size is to the canvas's shape:
792	
793	- **Within a pixel of the canvas's shape**, the picture fills the frame edge to edge, with no black line along an edge.
794	- **Any other shape** is letterboxed with black.
795	
796	Only **Custom…** can give you a different shape, because every row in the list has the canvas's shape.
797	
798	ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) don't letterbox, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. The sheet lets you choose the size, but Frame Job won't write the file: the export stops with a message naming the canvas and the size you asked for. Use a size with the canvas's proportions instead. An odd size typed in those proportions is fine. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).
799	
800	## Good to know
801	
802	- GIF and APNG fit the picture inside the size you choose, keeping its shape and never enlarging it, so they have no letterbox. Their rows show the fitted numbers: a 1080 × 1920 project's **GIF default** is 152 × 270. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/).
803	- **Size** is greyed out for the [audio-only formats](/export/audio-only/).
804	- A preset stores the row you chose rather than its numbers, so "4K" comes out at the right 4K size for each document. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).
805	
806	## With an agent
807	
808	An agent passes `size` to `export`: `document`, the default, then `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` for the GIF and APNG default, or `[width, height]` for a custom size. A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is an error. Every named size works on every document, including one the sheet hides as a repeat. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#size).
809

815	- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

817	title: Export frame rate
818	description: Export at the project's own frame rate, or at a fixed rate from 23.976 to 60 fps.
819	---
820	
821	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
822	
823	The **Frame rate** popup sets how many frames a second the exported file has, without changing the project.
824	
825	<AtAGlance
826	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
827	  keys="⌘E"
828	  where="Export sheet ▸ Frame rate"
829	  tools="export"
830	/>
831	
832	## Choose a frame rate
833	
834	Open the export sheet and pick a row in **Frame rate**. The readout under the controls shows the rate the file will have.
835	
836	**Project rate** is the default. It's the document's [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/), or the format's own rate for Animated GIF (12.5 fps) and Animated PNG (25 fps).
837	
838	The fixed rows, in the popup's order, are **24 fps**, **23.976 fps**, **25 fps**, **30 fps**, **29.97 fps**, **50 fps** and **60 fps**.
839	
840	Frame Job draws the same timeline at the new rate, so the export runs for the same length of time and only the number of frames changes.
841	
842	## What else the rate changes
843	
844	- **The range.** The start and length of the export are snapped to the export's frame grid, which moves each by less than a frame. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
845	- **The bit rate.** On **Format default** the video rate rises in step with the frame rate. The [Quality](/export/quality/) tiers rise by half above 30.5 fps, and each tier's title shows the new number.
846	- **The time an AV1 or VP9 export takes.** The estimate in the readout counts frames, so it follows the rate.
847	
848	## Good to know
849	
850	- **Frame rate** is greyed out for the [audio-only formats](/export/audio-only/), which have no frames.
851	- A fixed rate you export with is remembered with the rest of the sheet, and every document's sheet opens on it. Check it before you export a project with a different rate. Choose **Project rate** to go back. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
852	- A preset stores the rate you chose. **Project rate** stays **Project rate**, so it follows each document.
853	
854	## With an agent
855	
856	An agent can't set the frame rate. Its `export` uses the document's rate, or the format's own rate for GIF and APNG. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
857	
858	## Related
859	
860	- [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/)
861	- [Export size](/export/size/)

865	title: Encoder speed
866	description: Choose how long the AV1 encoder works on each frame, trading export time against file size.
867	---
868	
869	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
870	
871	The **Speed** row sets how long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. A longer time gives a smaller file, so it's a choice between waiting less and sending less.
872	
873	<AtAGlance
874	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
875	  keys="⌘E"
876	  where="Export sheet ▸ Speed"
877	  tools="export"
878	/>
879	
880	## Choose a speed
881	
882	In the export sheet, choose **AV1 (MP4)** or **AV1 (WebM)** in **Format**, then pick a row in **Speed**. The row sits under **Format**, or under **Dynamic Range** in an HDR project.
883	
884	| Speed | What it does | SVT-AV1 preset |
885	| --- | --- | --- |
886	| **Faster** | The quickest export and the largest file. | 8 |
887	| **Balanced** | The default. | 6 |
888	| **Smaller file** | The slowest export and the smallest file. | 4 |
889	
890	The footnote names your choice, for example `AV1 · MP4 · Balanced`, and the estimate in the readout follows it, for example `Estimated time: about 25 s`. The estimate is only a guide. Its figures come from an idle Apple M2 Max, so a slower or busy Mac, or a heavy timeline, takes longer.
891	
892	The rate from [Quality](/export/quality/) is the cap at every speed, and each speed is tuned to match HEVC's picture at that rate. So Speed moves the time and the file size, not the quality you asked for.
893	
894	## What each speed costs
895	
896	Measured on 10 seconds of 4K camera footage on an Apple M2 Max, exported as AV1 (MP4):
897	
898	| Speed | Time at 4K | File at 4K | Time at 1080p | File at 1080p |
899	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
900	| **Faster** | 7.1 s | 27 % larger | 2.4 s | 4 % larger |
901	| **Balanced** | 14.0 s | The baseline | 4.2 s | The baseline |
902	| **Smaller file** | 19.9 s | 12 % smaller | 5.8 s | 5 % smaller |
903	
904	The file size **Faster** adds is much greater at 4K than at 1080p, where it costs little.
905	
906	Speed changes the memory an export uses too. **Faster** measured about 1.3 GB at 1080p and 4.6 GB at 4K, **Balanced** about 2.2 GB and 7.5 GB, and **Smaller file** about 2.4 GB and 8.1 GB. AV1 and VP9 exports share a quarter of the Mac's memory, and a job that would go over it [waits for memory](/export/export-queue/#the-encoder-memory-wait) in the Export Queue.
907	
908	## Good to know
909	
910	- On every other format **Speed** is greyed out and keeps your last choice. That includes VP9 (WebM) and VP9 with Alpha (WebM), because VP9 has one speed.
911	- The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in [presets](/export/presets/).
912	
913	## With an agent
914	
915	An agent passes `encoder_speed` to `export`, as `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`. `balanced` is the default. It works on `av1` and `av1_webm` only, and any other format returns an error. The finished export's result names the speed used. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#encoder-speed).
916	
917	## Related
918	
919	- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)

923	title: Export quality
924	description: Set how many bits an export spends on its picture and sound, from Format default to the four tiers.
925	---
926	
927	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
928	
929	The **Quality** popup sets the data rate of the picture and the sound. A higher rate gives a better picture and a larger file.
930	
931	<AtAGlance
932	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
933	  keys="⌘E"
934	  where="Export sheet ▸ Quality"
935	  tools="export"
936	/>
937	
938	## Choose a quality
939	
940	Open the export sheet and pick a row in **Quality**: **Format default**, **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Maximum**. Each tier's title shows the rate it would ask for at the size and frame rate now chosen, for example `High · 8.0 Mbps`.
941	
942	Once you pick a tier, the footnote shows the rates too, for example `H264 · MP4 · 8.0 Mbps · 256 kbps audio`. With **Format default** it shows no rates.
943	
944	## Format default
945	
946	The default row. Frame Job works the rate out from the frame's size and rate:
947	
948	| Format | At 1080p, 30 fps | Bits per pixel per frame |
949	| --- | --- | --- |
950	| H.264 | About 8.7 Mbps | 0.14 |
951	| HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit | About 4.4 Mbps | 0.07 |
952	| AV1, VP9 | A [cap](#rates-on-av1-and-vp9) of about 4.4 Mbps | 0.07 |
953	
954	The rate rises in step with the frame's area and the frame rate, and it's held between 1 and 200 Mbps. So H.264 at 1080p is about 8.7 Mbps at 30 fps, a little above **High**, and about 17.4 Mbps at 60 fps, where **High** is 12.0 Mbps.
955	
956	The sound is 192 kbps AAC, or 192 kbps Opus in the WebM formats.
957	
958	## The four tiers
959	
960	Each tier sets the rate from the frame's size, so a tier means the same picture quality at every size. These are the H.264 rates at 30 fps or less:
961	
962	| Tier | Bits per pixel per frame | 720p | 1080p | 4K | Sound |
963	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
964	| **Low** | 0.064 | 1.8 Mbps | 4.0 Mbps | 15.9 Mbps | 128 kbps |
965	| **Medium** | 0.096 | 2.7 Mbps | 6.0 Mbps | 23.9 Mbps | 192 kbps |
966	| **High** | 0.129 | 3.6 Mbps | 8.0 Mbps | 32.1 Mbps | 256 kbps |
967	| **Maximum** | 0.193 | 5.3 Mbps | 12.0 Mbps | 48.0 Mbps | 320 kbps |
968	
969	A [preset](/export/presets/) stores the tier, not the number, so "High" works out the right rate on any document.
970	
971	## How the rate scales
972	
973	- **Frame size.** The rate scales with the frame's area, using the size you chose rather than the canvas's.
974	- **Frame rate.** Above 30.5 fps the rate is 1.5 times higher, so 50 and 60 fps are raised and 29.97 and 30 fps aren't. **High** at 1080p and 60 fps is 12.0 Mbps in H.264.
975	- **Codec.** HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate, so the HEVC formats ask for 60 % of it, and AV1 and VP9 use the same figure. **High** at 1080p is 4.8 Mbps in HEVC.
976	- **Rounding.** A rate is rounded to the nearest 100 kbps, and it never goes below 100 kbps.
977	
978	## Rates on AV1 and VP9
979	
980	On AV1 and VP9 the rate is a soft cap. The encoder works to a constant quality chosen to match HEVC at that rate, so the file usually stays under it. Very detailed footage can go over, by up to about 1.25 times the rate on AV1 and about 1.15 times on VP9.
981	
982	The tier titles and the footnote say so, for example `High · usually ≤ 4.8 Mbps`. AV1's cap stops at 100 Mbps, the most its encoder takes.
983	
984	On VP9 with Alpha (WebM) the rate covers the picture alone. The transparency is a second stream on top of it, so the file is larger than the rate says. See [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/).
985	
986	## Sound rates
987	
988	A tier sets the sound rate as well as the video rate.
989	
990	| Row | Sound |
991	| --- | --- |
992	| **Format default** | 192 kbps |
993	| **Low** | 128 kbps |
994	| **Medium** | 192 kbps |
995	| **High** | 256 kbps |
996	| **Maximum** | 320 kbps |
997	
998	The H.264, HEVC and AV1 (MP4) formats use these as AAC rates. The WebM formats ask the same rates of their Opus sound, rounded to the nearest rate the Opus encoder offers.
999	
1000	**Audio only (M4A)** has no picture, so a tier sets its AAC rate alone, and its titles read `High · 256 kbps`.
1001	
1002	## When Quality greys out
1003	
1004	**Quality** is greyed out for ProRes 422, ProRes 4444, WAV, AIFF, Animated GIF and Animated PNG, where the format fixes the rate. ProRes takes its rate from its profile and carries uncompressed sound, WAV and AIFF are uncompressed, and GIF and APNG have no rate at all.
1005	
1006	## With an agent
1007	
1008	An agent doesn't pick a tier. It passes `video_bitrate` and `audio_bitrate` to `export` in bits per second, so 8000000 is 8 Mbps, and leaving them out gives **Format default**. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore `video_bitrate`, and ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore `audio_bitrate`. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates).
1009	
1010	## Related

1013	- [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/)
1014	- [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/)
1015	- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
1016	- [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/)
1017	---
1018	title: Export bit depth
1019	description: Write a WAV or AIFF export at 16 or 24 bits.
1020	---
1021	
1022	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1023	
1024	The **Bit depth** row sets how finely a WAV or AIFF file records each sample of the sound. It's about sound only. The depth of the picture comes from the format you choose, and is on [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
1025	
1026	<AtAGlance
1027	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
1028	  keys="⌘E"
1029	  where="Export sheet ▸ Bit depth"
1030	  tools="export"
1031	/>
1032	
1033	## Choose a bit depth
1034	
1035	In the export sheet, choose **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)** in **Format**, then pick a row in **Bit depth**, which sits under **Quality**.
1036	
1037	| Row | What it's for |
1038	| --- | --- |
1039	| **16-bit** | The default. About 11.5 MB a minute. |
1040	| **24-bit** | Keeps detail 16-bit can't. It matters most for a quiet recording you're going to raise or process later. About 17.3 MB a minute. |
1041	
1042	A 24-bit file shows `24-bit` in the footnote, for example `LPCM · WAV · 24-bit`.
1043	
1044	Both depths are rounded once from the [float mix](/export/audio-only/#the-48-khz-stereo-master), to the nearest value, and neither is dithered.
1045	
1046	## Good to know
1047	
1048	- On every other format **Bit depth** is greyed out and keeps your last choice.
1049	- ProRes sound stays 16-bit, and AAC and Opus sound is encoded from 16-bit samples.
1050	- The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in [presets](/export/presets/).
1051	
1052	## With an agent
1053	
1054	An agent passes `audio_bits` to `export`, as 16 or 24. It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only, and any other format returns an error. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#audio-bits).
1055	
1056	## Related
1057	
1058	- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)
1059	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
1060	- [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/)

1	---
2	title: "Export a range"
3	description: Write only the part of the timeline between your in and out points, instead of the whole project.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An export writes the whole timeline unless you tell it otherwise. Use **Range:** on the export sheet to write only the passage between your in and out points, such as one section of a long project or a clip for review.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
13	  keys="⌘E"
14	  where="Export sheet ▸ Range"
15	  tools="export"
16	/>
17	
18	## Export only the range
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. On the timeline, set the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>.
23	
24	2. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.
25	
26	3. In **Range:**, choose **In/out range**.
27	
28	4. Check the length in the readout under the controls, then choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	## The Range popup
33	
34	| Choice | What it writes |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| **Whole project** | The whole timeline. This is the default. |
37	| **In/out range** | Only the range set on the timeline. It's listed only when a range is set. |
38	
39	With no range set, the popup is greyed out on **Whole project**.
40	
41	The range is rounded to whole frames at the export's rate and kept inside the project. If you change **Frame rate:**, it lands on that rate's frames, so its length can move by less than a frame. The readout always shows the length the file will have.
42	
43	The sheet remembers **In/out range** with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) can store it too. On a project with no range, either one falls back to **Whole project**.
44	
45	## Inside a nest
46	
47	An export always writes the top-level timeline, even when you're working inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). So it can't use a range that belongs to a nest.
48	
49	While a nest is open, the popup is greyed out on **Whole project**. If the nest has a range of its own, the popup's tooltip says why that range isn't offered.
50	
51	To export that passage, leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> and set the range on the timeline. A range stays with the timeline or nest it was set in, so opening or leaving a nest clears it.
52	
53	## Sound ends with the range
54	
55	A file's sound is exactly as long as the range it exports, including when a clip in it plays faster or slower. Frame Job cuts the sound at the range's end, and if the sound runs out early it fills the rest with silence.
56	
57	## Good to know
58	
59	- If a range turns out to be empty, for example one that lies past the end of the project after an edit, the sheet says the export range is empty and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** stay greyed out. Set the range again, or choose a different one.
60	- Animated GIF and Animated PNG files have a limit on their frame count, so a long range may not fit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/).
61	- [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/) reads project time, so a file from a range shows the timeline's timecode, not a count from zero.
62	- [Chapters](/export/chapters/) explains how a range export treats chapter markers.
63	
64	## With an agent
65	
66	`export` takes `range`: `project`, the default, or `in_out`, which writes the range set with `set_range`. With no range set, `in_out` gets an error instead of a file. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#range).
67	
68	## Related
69	
70	- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
71	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
72	- [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/)
73	- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
74	---
75	title: "Audio stems"
76	description: Write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix, for mixing or mastering in another editor.
77	---
78	
79	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
80	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
81	
82	An audio export can also write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix. These files are stems. Use them to mix or master the project in another editor.
83	
84	<AtAGlance
85	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
86	  keys="⌘E"
87	  where="Export sheet ▸ Stems"
88	  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
89	/>
90	
91	## Export stems
92	
93	<Steps>
94	
95	1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.
96	
97	2. In **Format:**, choose **Audio only (M4A)**, **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)**.
98	
99	3. In **Stems:**, choose **One per Track** or **One per Track Name**. The footnote on the sheet counts them, for example "3 stems".
100	
101	4. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**, then name the mix in the save panel.
102	
103	</Steps>
104	
105	Frame Job writes the mix, then each stem beside it. The stems are in the same format as the mix and cover the same range.
106	
107	## The Stems row
108	
109	| Choice | What it writes |
110	| --- | --- |
111	| **None** | The mix alone. This is the default. |
112	| **One per Track** | The mix, and one stem for each track you can hear. |
113	| **One per Track Name** | The mix, and one stem for each track name. |
114	
115	The row sits under **Bit depth:**. On every format except the three audio-only ones it's greyed out and keeps your last choice.
116	
117	The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.
118	
119	## Which tracks get a stem
120	
121	Only tracks you can hear get a stem:
122	
123	- A [muted track](/audio/mute-and-solo/) has no stem.
124	- While any track is soloed, only the soloed tracks have one.
125	- A track with no sound on it, only pictures or nothing, has none.
126	
127	With **One per Track Name**, tracks whose names match share one file. The match ignores case and any spaces at either end, and the file is named the way the first of those tracks is spelled. A track with no name gets its own file. Name your tracks in [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/).
128	
129	If no track can be heard, the sheet shows "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write", and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out.
130	
131	## Stem file names
132	
133	A stem is named after the mix and its track, and sits in the same folder. Exporting `Mix.wav` writes `Mix - Dialogue.wav` and `Mix - Music.wav`.
134	
135	| Case | The stem's name |
136	| --- | --- |
137	| A track with no name | Its header's label: `Mix - Track 3.wav` |
138	| A `/` or `:` in a track name | Written as `-` |
139	| A name an earlier stem already has, ignoring case | Its track's label follows: `Mix - vo (Track 2).wav` |
140	| That name is taken too | A count follows the label: `Mix - vo (Track 2, 2).wav` |
141	
142	No two stems share a file.
143	
144	## Overwriting and clean-up
145	
146	:::caution
147	An existing file at a stem's name is replaced without asking. The save panel asks only about the mix.
148	:::
149	
150	There's one exception. If a stem's file would be one of the project's own media files, the export stops before writing any stem and says so:
151	
152	> The stem “Mix - Dialogue.wav” would replace media this project uses; export under another name.
153	
154	The stems are written one after another after the mix, and the progress bar counts them. When it's done, the line reads "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems.", and its loudness figures are the mix's. A row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) ends its first sentence the same way.
155	
156	Cancelling, or a failure part-way, removes the mix and every stem already written.
157	
158	## Stems are pre-master
159	
160	The master is the export's last stage, where the loudness target and the master limiter work on the whole mix. Each stem holds its tracks' sound exactly as the mix plays it, but from before that stage:
161	
162	- It keeps the clips' and tracks' volume, pan, fades, ducking and effects, and a track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
163	- It gets no [loudness target](/export/loudness/), and the [master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) doesn't touch it.
164	
165	So the stems added together are the mix, to within rounding, wherever the master neither raised the level nor limited a peak.
166	
167	A stem can peak higher than the mix. It's clipped only at full scale.
168	
169	## Good to know
170	
171	A stem has no [chapters](/export/chapters/), even in an M4A file. Only the mix carries them.
172	
173	## With an agent
174	
175	`export` takes `stems`: `tracks` for **One per Track**, or `names` for **One per Track Name**. It works on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other format, or when no track can be heard, `export` returns an error and writes nothing. When the job is done, `export_status` lists each stem's name, tracks and path. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#stems).
176	
177	## Related
178	
179	- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)
180	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
181	- [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/)
182	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
183	- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)

185	title: "Export loudness"
186	description: Normalise a whole mix to a loudness target, and read what every export reports about its sound.
187	---
188	
189	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
190	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
191	
192	Streaming services, podcast hosts and broadcasters each ask for a certain loudness. **Loudness:** on the export sheet makes the whole mix land on that target, and every export tells you what its sound measured, whether you normalised it or not.
193	
194	<AtAGlance
195	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
196	  keys="⌘E"
197	  where="Export sheet ▸ Loudness"
198	  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
199	/>
200	
201	## Hit a loudness target
202	
203	<Steps>
204	
205	1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.
206	
207	2. In **Loudness:**, choose a target. The footnote on the sheet shows it, for example "−14 LUFS".
208	
209	3. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.
210	
211	4. When the file is done, read [the loudness line](#what-the-loudness-line-means) to see what it measured.
212	
213	</Steps>
214	
215	## The Loudness popup
216	
217	The target is the integrated loudness of the whole mix: one figure for the file from start to end, in LUFS, measured to ITU-R BS.1770-4.
218	
219	| Choice | What it's for |
220	| --- | --- |
221	| **Off** | No normalisation. The export still goes through the master limiter, measures its sound and reports it. |
222	| **−14 LUFS (streaming)** | Where the main streaming services normalise. |
223	| **−16 LUFS** | The usual target for stereo podcasts. |
224	| **−23 LUFS (broadcast)** | EBU R 128 broadcast delivery. |
225	| **Custom…** | Any target you type in the field beside the popup, from −70 to 0 LUFS, to one decimal place. |
226	
227	The popup works on every format with sound, ProRes included. It's greyed out for Animated GIF and Animated PNG, which have no sound.
228	
229	With **Custom…**, the field starts from the target you had chosen, or −14 after **Off**. While it's empty, the sheet says "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list." and **Export…** is greyed out.
230	
231	The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.
232	
233	## How normalisation works
234	
235	The export measures the real mix first, then applies **one gain** to everything. Levels inside the timeline keep their relationship to each other, so a quiet line stays quieter than a loud one.
236	
237	The progress line reads "Measuring loudness…" during this pass. It fills the first tenth of the progress bar on a movie export, and the first half on an audio-only one.
238	
239	The gain is worked out through the master limiter, so the file lands on the target even when its loudest peaks would pass the ceiling. Those peaks are turned down, not the whole mix.
240	
241	The gain can be at most +40 dB, so a target more than 40 dB above the mix lands quieter than you asked. It's rounded to 0.01 dB, so two exports of one project get the same gain.
242	
243	## The master limiter
244	
245	Every export with sound goes through a true-peak limiter, normalised or not. True peak is the highest the sound really reaches, including between samples, and dBTP is its unit. The limiter keeps the file's true peak at or under **−1 dBTP**. A mix that would pass that is limited instead of clipped, whether the cause is loud clips, a crossfade between two loud clips, a nest turned up or an action that raises a clip's volume.
246	
247	- Sound under the ceiling passes through untouched, sample for sample.
248	- The limiter holds the sound back 3.3 ms to see each peak coming, and releases over 100 ms. The export takes that delay back, so the sound stays exactly in sync with the picture.
249	- You can't turn it off, and the sheet fixes the ceiling at −1 dBTP.
250	
251	:::note
252	The preview has no master limiter, so a mix that passes −1 dBTP sounds louder while you edit than it does in the file.
253	:::
254	
255	## Track compressors in the export
256	
257	A track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) run before the master, on that track's sound alone, exactly as you set them. The export plays each such track on its own through them and mixes the tracks afterwards.
258	
259	The measurement for a loudness target hears them too, so the file still lands on the target. A [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them.
260	
261	The master is only the loudness gain and the limiter. There's no master compressor or EQ. To compress the whole mix, [nest](/editing/nests/) everything onto one track and give that track a compressor.
262	
263	## What the loudness line means
264	
265	Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured, on the [finish line](/export/progress-and-report/#the-finish-report) and in its [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) row.
266	
267	| Line | What it means |
268	| --- | --- |
269	| `Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS` | The true peak and integrated loudness of the file. |
270	| `Peak … · loudness not measurable` | The sound is too short or too quiet to have a loudness. It needs at least 0.4 s. |
271	| `Silent` | The sound is digital silence. |
272	| `… · peaks limited by 8.6 dB` | The master limiter turned the loudest peak down by that much to hold the ceiling. It appears from 0.05 dB. |
273	| `Peak not measurable (a non-finite sample in the mix)` | A source file holds a sample that isn't a number, so no gain is applied. |
274	
275	A large "peaks limited by" figure on music can be audible. Turn the clips down, or ask for a lower target.
276	
277	## Good to know
278	
279	- Sound with no loudness to measure gets no gain, so a target has no effect on digital silence or on sound that's too short or too quiet.
280	- If the sound can't be measured at all, the file is written without normalisation and the line has no figures. A timeline with no sound at all has none either.
281	- The figures describe the mix. Stems aren't measured, and they get no target or master limiter.
282	
283	## With an agent
284	
285	`export` takes the target as `loudness_lufs`, any value from −70 to 0, and ignores it on `gif` and `apng`.
286	
287	An agent can also choose a different ceiling for the master limiter with `peak_dbtp`, which the sheet doesn't offer. It runs from −20 to 0 dBTP, is −1 when left out, and works with or without a target. 0 dBTP is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
288	
289	`export_status` returns the line's figures as numbers in `loudness`, and `capped_by_gain` says when the +40 dB limit decided the gain. See [The loudness report](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report).
290	
291	## Related
292	
293	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
294	- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
295	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
296	- [Audio stems](/export/stems/)
297	- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)
298	- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)

300	title: "Burn in timecode"
301	description: Draw the project's timecode into an exported picture, so a reviewer's notes point at exact frames.
302	---
303	
304	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
305	
306	Burn in timecode draws the project's timecode into the exported picture. Use it for a review copy, so a note about a frame carries the number you'll find on your timeline.
307	
308	<AtAGlance
309	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
310	  keys="⌘E"
311	  where="Export sheet ▸ Burn in timecode"
312	  tools={['export', 'render_frame']}
313	/>
314	
315	## Burn in timecode
316	
317	Choose **File ▸ Export…** and turn on **Burn in timecode**. It's off by default.
318	
319	The timecode appears only in the exported file, never in the preview. It sits centred near the bottom of the picture, on a translucent black plate, on top of everything, captions included.
320	
321	The box works on every format with a picture, Animated GIF and Animated PNG included. It's greyed out for the audio-only formats, and **File ▸ Save Frame…** never offers it.
322	
323	The sheet remembers it with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.
324	
325	## What the timecode shows
326	
327	It uses the project's own timecode format, as the toolbar shows it: `HH:MM:SS:FF` or `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, non-drop. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
328	
329	It shows **project time**. A file exported from an [in/out range](/export/range/) that starts at 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 in a player, but its first frame reads 00:00:10:00. That's the number a reviewer's note needs.
330	
331	## With an agent
332	
333	`burn_in_timecode` turns it on in `export`, and it's off by default. `render_frame` takes the same argument, so an agent can draw the timecode into a single frame, which **Save Frame…** can't do. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
334	
335	## Related
336	
337	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
338	- [Export a range](/export/range/)
339	- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
340	- [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/)

342	title: "Export presets"
343	description: Save the export sheet's choices under a name, and set the whole sheet with one pick in any project.
344	---
345	
346	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
347	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
348	
349	A preset is a set of export choices you've saved under a name. Pick it and the whole sheet is set, in any project. It's the quick way back to the export you make every week.
350	
351	<AtAGlance
352	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
353	  keys="⌘E"
354	  where={['Export sheet ▸ Preset', 'Export sheet ▸ the gear beside Preset']}
355	/>
356	
357	## Apply a preset
358	
359	Pick the preset in **Preset:**. Every control is set exactly as if you had clicked it.
360	
361	The first row is **Custom**, then your presets. Picking **Custom** leaves the sheet as it is. The gear beside the popup saves and deletes presets.
362	
363	## Save a preset
364	
365	<Steps>
366	
367	1. Set the sheet the way you want it.
368	
369	2. Click the gear beside **Preset:** and choose **Save…**.
370	
371	3. Type a name and click **Save**, or **Cancel** to save nothing. The name field starts with the name of the preset now chosen.
372	
373	</Steps>
374	
375	Saving under a name that already exists, ignoring case, replaces that preset in its place in the list. New presets go at the end.
376	
377	Frame Job beeps and saves nothing when:
378	
379	- The name is empty.
380	- The name is **Custom**, in any case. It's reserved for the popup's first row.
381	- The sheet has an error, for example an empty custom field.
382	- The presets file can't be written.
383	
384	## Change a preset
385	
386	Apply it, adjust the controls, and save again under the same name. There's no separate rename: to rename a preset, save it under the new name and delete the old one.
387	
388	## Delete a preset
389	
390	Choose the preset in **Preset:**, then choose **Delete** from the gear. **Delete** is available only while a saved preset is chosen, and it doesn't ask you to confirm.
391	
392	The controls keep the preset's values, so **Save…** under the same name puts it back. It returns at the end of the list.
393	
394	## What a preset stores
395	
396	A preset stores the choices on the sheet, not the numbers they resolve to, so it means the same on a project of another size. A preset saved on a 1080p project that says "4K, High" exports at the right 4K size and bit rate on any other project.
397	
398	It stores:
399	
400	- Format
401	- Size row, or the custom size
402	- Frame rate
403	- Quality tier
404	- Loudness
405	- Range
406	- Burn in timecode
407	- Speed
408	- Bit depth
409	- Stems
410	
411	**Dynamic Range** isn't stored.
412	
413	The format decides what a preset can hold. Size, frame rate, quality, loudness and burn-in aren't stored when the format can't use them, so a preset saved on an audio-only format has no size, and one saved on Animated GIF has no loudness. Applying it puts those controls back on their defaults. Speed, Bit depth and Stems are stored whichever format is chosen.
414	
415	When a preset meets a different project:
416	
417	- A range falls back to **Whole project** if the project has no range.
418	- A size row hidden on this project, because an earlier row has the same numbers, lands on that earlier row. A size row the format doesn't offer falls back to the format's default.
419	- A custom size stays those exact numbers.
420	
421	## Back to Custom
422	
423	Changing **Format:**, **Size:**, **Frame rate:**, **Quality:**, **Loudness:**, **Range:**, **Burn in timecode** or a custom field puts the popup back on **Custom**. Changing the value back doesn't select the preset again.
424	
425	**Speed:**, **Bit depth:** and **Stems:** don't do this. After you change one of those three, the popup still shows the preset's name, even though the sheet no longer matches it.
426	
427	The popup opens on **Custom** each time, even when your remembered choices happen to match a preset.
428	
429	## The presets file
430	
431	Presets are kept for your macOS user account, so every project and window shares them. They live in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json`.
432	
433	You can open the file in a text editor. A damaged file reads as no presets, and the export sheet works as usual.
434	
435	Saving or deleting reads the file first, so two open sheets can't lose each other's presets. A sheet that's already open keeps listing a preset you've deleted elsewhere until it saves or deletes a preset itself, or you open it again.
436	
437	## Transparent presets
438	
439	A preset on a transparent format, such as **ProRes 4444 (MOV)** or **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**, stores the format and nothing about the canvas. The file is transparent only when the project's canvas background is. A custom size also has to match the canvas's shape on these formats, so a preset with a custom size can fail on a canvas of another shape. Use a size row instead, because the rows fit each project's shape. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).
440	
441	## With an agent
442	
443	Presets belong to the sheet, and `export` doesn't read them. Its `preset` argument is something else: it names the format, and the call sets each other choice itself. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
444

453	title: "Export progress and the report"
454	description: Follow an export as it writes, cancel it, read its finish report, and find out why one failed.
455	---
456	
457	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
458	
459	After you choose **Export…** on the export sheet, Frame Job asks where to save, then writes the file behind a progress sheet. When it's done, the sheet tells you what the sound measured and what went wrong, if anything did.
460	
461	<AtAGlance
462	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
463	  keys="⌘E"
464	  where="The Exporting sheet"
465	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
466	/>
467	
468	**Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then writes the file behind the editor so you can keep working. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
469	
470	## The save panel
471	
472	The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written:
473	
474	| Format | Message |
475	| --- | --- |
476	| A movie | "Export the timeline as a movie." |
477	| Animated GIF | "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." |
478	| Animated PNG | "Export the timeline as an animated APNG." |
479	| Audio only | "Export the timeline's audio." |
480	
481	Cancelling the save panel writes nothing. The export sheet has already closed by then, and it keeps the choices you made for next time.
482	
483	## The Exporting sheet
484	
485	**Exporting** shows a progress bar, a percentage and a status line. The status line moves through these:
486	
487	| Status line | What's happening |
488	| --- | --- |
489	| "Preparing “*name*”…" | Frame Job is getting everything ready, and may be waiting for something the file needs. |
490	| "Measuring loudness…" | The sound is being [measured](/export/loudness/#how-normalisation-works). Every export with sound does this, whether or not you chose a target. |
491	| "Writing “*name*”…" | The file is being written. |
492	
493	The file is written from the timeline as it was when you confirmed it.
494	
495	### While it says Preparing
496	
497	Some of what a file holds has to be made first, so the export waits for it:
498	
499	- The masks of every [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/#exports) clip in the range, with no time limit.
500	- Each clip's pointer, from its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
501	- The measured loudness of every clip with a gate, leveller or de-esser, for up to five minutes.
502	- The rendered sound of speed changes, Voice Isolation and voice effects.
503	
504	GIF and APNG files have no sound, so they don't wait for the last two. You can cancel during any of these waits. [Waiting for what it needs](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs) lists which clips each wait covers, and what happens if something can't be made.
505	
506	## Cancel a running export
507	
508	Choose **Cancel**. The button greys out while the export stops, then the sheet closes and the half-written file is removed.
509	
510	:::caution
511	If you chose to replace an existing file in the save panel, that file is gone once you cancel. Cancelling doesn't bring it back.
512	:::
513	
514	## The finish report
515	
516	When an export finishes, the status line names the file and says what the sound measured:
517	
518	> Exported “name.mp4”. Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS.
519	
520	[What the loudness line means](/export/loudness/#what-the-loudness-line-means) explains those figures. A file with no sound has no figures. An export with [stems](/export/stems/) counts them after the name: "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems."
521	
522	**Show in Finder** reveals the file and closes the sheet. **Close** closes the sheet.
523	
524	## Graphic and cursor warnings
525	
526	A warning doesn't stop an export. The finish line adds a count, and its tooltip lists each warning.
527	
528	| Warning | What happened | What the tooltip lists |
529	| --- | --- | --- |
530	| "1 graphic warning (hover for details)." | A [graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) warned while the file was drawn. | Each warning, with the graphic's name and its frame. |
531	| "1 cursor warning (hover for details)." | A clip's cursor file couldn't be drawn, so that clip is written without its pointer. | Each one, for example "The cursor of media 3 is not drawn: …" |
532	
533	The cursor count comes after the graphic count. A finished row in the Export Queue shows the same counts, and its tooltip lists the same warnings.
534	
535	## Failures
536	
537	**File ▸ Export…** is greyed out while the timeline is empty. Any other export that can't run says why in a sentence, on the sheet or on its queue row. On the sheet, **Close** dismisses it.
538	
539	| The sheet says | What to do |
540	| --- | --- |
541	| "The export was not started: the graphic …" | A graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module. Fix it and export again. |
542	| "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic …" | A graphic failed at that frame. No file is left. |
543	| "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs that measurement. Wait for the **Status** rows in those sections to show the clip's loudness, then export again. |
544	| "Clip …'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | The sound of a speed change couldn't be made. |
545	| "Clip …'s isolated voice could not be rendered: …" | Voice Isolation couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
546	| "Clip …'s voice effect could not be rendered: …" | The voice effect couldn't be rendered for that clip. |
547	| "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …" or "Clip …'s foreground masks could not be made: …" | A Remove Background clip's masks failed. No frame is written without them. |
548	| "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose another format. No file is left. |
549	| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | A custom size has a different shape from the canvas. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |
550	
551	Other messages come from macOS or the file being written, and appear as they are.
552	
553	A failure is different from a cancel. A failed Animated GIF, Animated PNG or WebM export removes its partly written file, and so does a failed export with stems. Any other format that fails while writing can leave a partly written file at the path you chose. It isn't a finished export, so delete it.
554	
555	## Quitting during an export
556	
557	Quitting while the Exporting sheet is writing doesn't ask, and can leave the half-written file behind. Cancel the export first.
558	
559	Only the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) is guarded at quit, so jobs there ask before they stop.
560	
561	## With an agent
562	
563	An agent's `export` puts a job on the Export Queue and returns at once, with no progress sheet. A bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline or a graphic that doesn't compile comes back from `export` before anything is queued. Failures while writing and the loudness figures come back from `export_status`, and `cancel_export` stops the job.
564	
565	Warnings arrive in the finished `export_status` as `graphic_warnings` and `cursor_warnings`, and are left out when there are none. The list of graphic warnings stops after 64 distinct ones. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
566

576	title: "The Export Queue"
577	description: "Write exports behind the editor, one at a time, while you keep working, and follow, cancel or reveal each one from a single window."
578	---
579	
580	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
581	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
582	
583	The Export Queue writes the same file as **Export…** without making you wait for it. Jobs run one at a time behind the editor while you keep working.
584	
585	<AtAGlance
586	  menu="Window ▸ Export Queue"
587	  where="Export sheet ▸ Add to Queue"
588	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
589	/>
590	
591	## Add to Queue
592	
593	<Steps>
594	
595	1. Set up the file in the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
596	
597	2. Choose **Add to Queue**. It's available whenever **Export…** is.
598	
599	3. Name the file in the save panel and choose **Save**. This is the same panel **Export…** opens.
600	
601	</Steps>
602	
603	The **Export Queue** window then opens on its own, with the job in it. Your settings are remembered as the last choice, as they are for **Export…**.
604	
605	Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** no progress sheet is in the way. You can start playback again and go on editing while the job runs.
606	
607	## The Export Queue window
608	
609	Choose **Window ▸ Export Queue** to open it at any time. It has no keyboard shortcut.
610	
611	The window lists every queued, running and finished export. Jobs run one at a time, in the order they were added, unless a job has to [wait for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). Closing the window stops nothing. Open it again and the jobs are where they'd got to.
612	
613	The line at the bottom counts the jobs, for example "1 exporting · 2 waiting · 3 finished". With nothing in the list, the window reads "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."
614	
615	The list isn't saved. It starts empty each time you open Frame Job.
616	
617	## Rows and their states
618	
619	Each row shows the file's name and where the job has got to.
620	
621	| The row says | What it means | Button |
622	| --- | --- | --- |
623	| `Waiting` | Queued behind the running job. | **Cancel** |
624	| `Waiting for memory: …` | An AV1 or VP9 job [waiting for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). | **Cancel** |
625	| `Writing · 42 %` | The job is running, with a progress bar beside it. It can stay at `Writing · 0 %` while the job [waits for what it needs](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs). | **Cancel** |
626	| `Measuring loudness… · 12 %` | The job is measuring the mix before it writes. | **Cancel** |
627	| `Stopping…` | You cancelled the job and it hasn't stopped yet. | **Cancel** |
628	| `Exported “Board.mp4”.` | The file was written. Any stems, graphic warnings and cursor warnings are counted after the name, then come the [loudness figures](/export/progress-and-report/). | **Show**, **Remove** |
629	| `Overwritten by a later export to the same file.` | The job finished, but a later job has since started writing to the same path. | **Remove** |
630	| `Cancelled.` | You stopped it while it ran. | **Remove** |
631	| `Cancelled before it started.` | You stopped it while it waited. | **Remove** |
632	| The reason it failed | The job stopped with an error. | **Remove** |
633	
634	Hold the pointer over a row for its tooltip: the full path, the container, the size and the frame rate, then the whole memory sentence while a job waits for memory, then each graphic and cursor warning.
635	
636	| Button | What it does |
637	| --- | --- |
638	| **Cancel** | Stops that job and removes its half-written file. A waiting job is cancelled before it starts. |
639	| **Remove** | Takes a finished row out of the list. The file stays where it is. |
640	| **Show** | Reveals the finished file in the Finder. If the file has since been moved or deleted, Frame Job beeps. |
641	
642	## Clear Finished and Cancel All
643	
644	**Clear Finished** removes every finished, cancelled and failed row and leaves the queue running. It's dimmed when there's nothing to clear, and it deletes no files.
645	
646	**Cancel All** stops the running job and every waiting one. It's dimmed when nothing is running or waiting.
647	
648	A cancelled job's half-written file is removed. The queue doesn't delete a failed job's file, so a part-written file can be left where you saved it.
649	
650	## A queued job's snapshot
651	
652	A job holds the timeline as it was when you chose **Save** in the save panel, including its media files, reversed clips, graphics, chapters and any timecode burn-in.
653	
654	Edits, undos and relinks made afterwards don't change what it writes, and neither does closing the document. You can queue one version, go on cutting, and queue another.
655	
656	## Quit with jobs in the queue
657	
658	Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first, after Frame Job has asked about any unsaved documents.
659	
660	The alert reads "An export is still being written." and names the running file, for example "“Board.mp4” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting. Quitting now stops it and deletes the partly written file."
661	
662	- **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue, deletes the partly written file and quits.
663	- **Cancel** keeps Frame Job open and the queue running.
664	
665	:::caution
666	Only the queue is guarded this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel that export first.
667	:::
668	
669	## The encoder memory wait
670	
671	AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, and they use a lot of memory.
672	
673	| Format | At 1080p | At 4K |
674	| --- | --- | --- |
675	| AV1 (MP4) and AV1 (WebM), depending on [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) | About 1.2–2.4 GB | About 4.4–8.1 GB |
676	| VP9 (WebM) | About 0.4–0.5 GB | About 1.1–1.6 GB |
677	| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | About 0.7 GB | About 2.2 GB |
678	
679	All the AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may hold up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. On a 16 GB Mac that's 4.0 GB.
680	
681	A queued AV1 or VP9 job starts only if it fits in that quarter with what's already running. The queue itself runs one job at a time, so what holds a job back is an AV1 or VP9 export running behind an **Export…** progress sheet.
682	
683	- When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large.
684	- While a job waits, a later job that fits runs first, and so does any job in a format the Mac encodes itself, such as H.264 or ProRes.
685	- An **Export…** sheet never waits. It's counted and starts straight away, so several sheets at once can go past the quarter.
686	
687	The row's status is one line, so the sentence usually ends in "…" before its figures. The tooltip ends with all of it: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB."
688	
689	The figures are measured, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more.
690	
691	## Good to know
692	
693	- **Export…** doesn't join the queue. It writes straight away behind its [own progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/), and it can run while a queued job runs.
694	- Two jobs can name the same file. The save panel asks about replacing a file only if it's already on disk, so two quick **Add to Queue** choices with one name may not ask at all. The later job replaces the file as it starts writing, whether or not it goes on to finish, and the earlier row stops offering **Show**.
695	
696	## With an agent
697	
698	An agent's `export` always goes through the queue, never a progress sheet. Its job is a row like any other, but the window doesn't open on its own. `export_status` reads that row, including the memory sentence while the job waits, and `cancel_export` is its **Cancel**, though a running job can still read `running` until writing has stopped. An agent can follow and stop only the jobs it started. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

712	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
713	
714	Save Frame writes the frame under the playhead to a still image: a thumbnail, a poster frame or a picture for a document.
715	
716	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Save Frame…" keys="⌥⌘E" tools="render_frame" />
717	
718	## Save a frame
719	
720	<Steps>
721	
722	1. Move the playhead to the frame.
723	
724	2. Choose **File ▸ Save Frame…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>. It's greyed out while the timeline is empty.
725	
726	3. Pick a **Format:** and a place. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` in place of `:`, such as `Board 00-00-12-05.png`.
727	
728	4. Choose **Save**.
729	
730	</Steps>
731	
732	The frame is the one the playhead was on when you opened the panel. When the save works, nothing else appears. The file is where you put it.
733	
734	If it doesn't work, an alert says why:
735	
736	| The alert says | What it means |
737	| --- | --- |
738	| "There is no frame at the playhead. The time is past the end of the timeline, the timeline is empty, or the media is missing." | Frame Job couldn't draw a frame at that time. |
739	| "Could not write PNG to … The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it." | The folder is missing, or Frame Job can't write into it. |
740	| "Could not write HEIC to … This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format." | This Mac has no encoder for the format. |
741	
742	## PNG, JPEG or HEIC
743	
744	| **Format:** | File | Transparency | Depth | Compression |
745	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
746	| **PNG** | `.png` | Kept | 8-bit, or 16-bit for a [deep frame](#deep-and-hdr-frames) | Lossless |
747	| **JPEG** | `.jpg` | None. A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. | Always 8-bit | 90 % quality |
748	| **HEIC** | `.heic` | Kept | 8-bit, or 10-bit for a deep frame | 90 % quality |
749	
750	The popup opens on **PNG** every time and doesn't remember your last choice. A line under it says what the chosen format does with transparency, such as "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
751	
752	Choosing a format changes the extension in the file name and keeps a name you've typed. Only `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` and `.heic` count as extensions, so `Board v1.2` keeps its `.2` and becomes `Board v1.2.jpg`.
753	
754	## Drawn the way an export draws it
755	
756	The frame is drawn the way an [export](/export/what-an-export-includes/) draws it, at the canvas's full size.
757	
758	Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version and Show Selection never change it. It never carries a timecode burn-in, even if you use one on your exports.
759	
760	## Inside a nest
761	
762	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the saved frame is the picture the canvas is showing: the nest's own, at the nest's size and the nest's time. The timecode in the suggested name is the nest's too. Save Frame is greyed out in an empty nest, however full the timeline is.
763	
764	This is the opposite of an export, which always writes the whole timeline.
765	
766	## Deep and HDR frames
767	
768	Most frames are saved at 8 bits a channel and labelled BT.709. These are saved with more:
769	
770	- **A deep frame.** A frame showing a still deeper than 8 bits, or a 10-bit VP9 clip, is saved as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, still labelled BT.709. A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip is saved deep too, when every video track in the timeline is that deep.
771	- **An [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/).** Every PNG and HEIC keeps the HLG picture, as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG.
772	
773	JPEG is always 8-bit. In an HDR project a JPEG is the project's [SDR version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), labelled BT.709.
774	
775	See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/) for how depth runs through the rest of the app.
776	
777	## Waiting for masks
778	
779	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 seconds for that frame's masks, which are made on this Mac. Past that, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the clip's file, for example "speech.mov drawn whole: the person masks were not ready within 30 seconds."
780	
781	Save the frame again once the clip's **Status** row shows the masks are done. An export never does this: it [waits as long as the masks take](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs).
782	
783	## Good to know
784	
785	A graphic that fails draws its error card in the saved frame, and a clip whose cursor file can't be read is drawn without its cursor. Save Frame doesn't warn you about either, so look at the picture.
786	
787	## The same still for an agent
788	
789	`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame for the same frame and format. It returns the picture itself as well as a file, and with no path it writes a temporary PNG and names it. The format comes from `format` if you pass it, otherwise from the path's extension, otherwise PNG.
790	
791	It also reports what Save Frame keeps quiet: when a graphic in the frame warned or failed it names the graphic, its frame and the message, and it names a cursor file it couldn't read. Like Save Frame, it waits 30 seconds for masks and says which clip it drew whole. An agent can ask for more than the menu offers, such as a timecode burn-in, an ungraded picture or scope measurements. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

808	A transparent canvas lets you export a title, a lower third or an overlay that sits on top of something else. Only four formats keep the transparency, so the format is the choice that matters.

811	  where={['Document tab ▸ Appearance ▸ Background', 'Export sheet ▸ Format']}
